confidence_notes: The restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from crowd-sourced cost-of-living figures found by web search. MyLifeElsewhere lists an inexpensive meal at about $8, a domestic pint at about $2.40 and a cappuccino at about $2.36. Traveltables' July 2023 data lists a meal at $7.30, a 0.5 L draught beer at $2.58, a cappuccino at $1.67 and a three-course mid-range meal for two at about $62. Because the Traveltables data is older, all of these were nudged up slightly for a 2026 tourist-zone basis. The cocktail and wine anchors are less certain. Searches found 2026 Bávaro bar guides putting off-resort cocktails at about $6-12, with beach-bar beer at $3-5. No reliable aggregated price for a glass of wine was found, so the wine anchor is estimated from local bottle prices and its usual relationship to beer and cocktail prices. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates only; no booking pages or listings were checked. Punta Cana is dominated by all-inclusive resorts and has very few registered hostels, so the hostel anchors are especially uncertain. They assume a few Bávaro-area hostels and guesthouses at Caribbean-tourist price levels, for July (shoulder/low season).
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are based on Punta Cana/Bávaro cost-of-living aggregates, adjusted toward Caribbean beach-resort price levels. These are higher than Santo Domingo and comparable to Cancún or Playa del Carmen for accommodation and drinks.
